boundaries.note: The Premier League bottom club is relegated and the First Division's top two are 'offered' promotion, but a Premier League place requires the HKFA club licence and a professional set-up, so in most seasons fewer clubs go up than are entitled to.
First Division: bottom two down. Second Division: top two of the Championship Group up, bottom two of the Challenging Group down.

conflicts.real: 16 clubs in 2026-27, split 8/8; the competition-format text describes an 8+7 split because it was written for a 15-club season
conflicts.note: The single-round-robin-then-split shape is right; the group sizes follow the entry list, so they change with promotions and withdrawals.

No HKFA U22 league article could be found; the HKFA runs age-group competitions alongside the senior pyramid (the U22-minute quota used to be enforced through the Sapling Cup, discontinued after 2025-26). Treat the row as an age-group competition with no promotion route; size 11 is our value, unverified.

notes: Four senior levels, all run by the HKFA: Premier League (11), First Division (14), Second Division (16), Third Division (not in our rows, and its bottom club leaves the system entirely). The Premier League's promotion door is a licence, not a table position - First Division clubs are 'offered' promotion and regularly decline or fail licensing, which is why the top flight sat at 11 clubs in 2026-27 after Sha Tin went up. Second Division plays a single round robin (15 games) then splits into an 8-team Championship Group and an 8-team Challenging Group for seven more games. HK22 is an age-group competition: closed in both directions by definition, and reserve/youth sides cannot move into the senior pyramid.
